name: Brian Eno
hook: A non-musician by his own description who used the synthesizer and the tape recorder to invent ambient music and to rebuild how Bowie made records.
blurb: Brian Eno joined Roxy Music in 1971, where he treated the band's sound through an EMS VCS3 synthesizer. After leaving in 1973 he made his own records, including slow, quiet music made with tape loops that he called ambient. What he gave music was more a method than a sound: tape loops of different lengths so the music never repeats exactly, systems that make music with little input, and the Oblique Strategies cards he made with Peter Schmidt. In 1976 he recorded with Harmonia, Michael Rother's band, just before working with David Bowie on Low and 'Heroes' (1976 and 1977), which ties the German scene to Bowie's albums directly. His Bowie role is often misstated: Tony Visconti co-produced those albums with Bowie, and Eno was a collaborator and co-writer. He went on to produce Talking Heads and U2.
